raised.value: $80M total funding to date, including an $18M Series A in 2023 backed by Peter Thiel

entry.idea: Lindus Health runs clinical trials for biotech and pharma companies, using its own technology and in-house team to recruit patients and manage data faster than a traditional research organisation.
entry.lesson: Once you get very good at the hard, unglamorous middle step of an industry (running the trials), you can move up the value chain and own the end product instead of only servicing the companies that do.
entry.name: Lindus Health

growth.reason: Total funding has grown from an $18M Series A in 2023 to $80M today, alongside 45+ completed trials and two years running on a national Top 100 startup list.

market.reason: Every pharma and biotech company in the world needs clinical trials run, and the market for developing new medicines is enormous.

tech.reason: It uses AI-powered patient search and an integrated in-house team to speed up trial recruitment, a real edge but one a well-funded rival could match in a year or two.

entry.twist: It has grown from running other companies' trials into buying the rights to promising drugs itself and developing them, using that same trial-running expertise.
entry.who_pays: Biotech and pharma companies pay Lindus to run their clinical trials, and Lindus is now also funding its own drug-licensing deals from its balance sheet.
entry.why_now: Clinical trials are usually slow and expensive, and Lindus says its in-house recruitment technology lets most of its trials finish on time or early.
